summary: The reseller settlement leg for an uncaptured sale — the half of the partner API that was descoped
description:
**Filed 2026-08-25 by a backlog review. TKT-240 parked this on TKT-23, an undecomposed epic; it had no discrete ticket.**

TKT-240 shipped a reseller API in which a partner authenticates, is confined by its credential, and **can read its own availability** — and cannot sell. Its own closeout is explicit:

> The COS row "The partner may hold and confirm a sale" — **NOT MET — descoped.**
> TKT-23 (or a new child) must define the settlement leg for a sale that was never captured, which means amending ADR-048. That is a **larger piece of work than everything else in this ticket**.

**Why it needs its own ticket.** It was carried as a `kind=blocker` comment on **TKT-23**, which is an epic in Backlog whose own description says *"Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic."* So the largest known gap in a shipped feature is parked on a container that, by its own terms, is not being decomposed yet. A reader of the board sees a delivered reseller API; the fact that it cannot complete a sale is one comment deep on an unrelated epic.

**The substance.** A reseller sale is not the buyer flow with a different credential: the partner takes the money (or does not), so the platform books a sale for which it never captured funds. ADR-048 (settlement ledger) has no representation for that today, which is why TKT-240 removed the capability after building it rather than shipping a false claim.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ADR-048 is amended (or a new ADR recorded) defining how an uncaptured reseller sale settles: what the ledger records, what the platform is owed, and what the partner owes — money as integer minor units, no fabricated money facts (ADR-003: the journal records what happened, not what didn't).
- [ ] The partner hold + confirm path exists behind `PartnerCredential`, confined to the partner's own channel allocation (ADR-056, ADR-060).
- [ ] Reseller-scoped idempotency, so a partner's retry cannot double-sell.
- [ ] A test proves a partner sale consumes its own channel's allocation and no other's — asserted in the store under the pool lock, which is where the mechanism lives (ADR-010, and AGENTS.md on test tiers).

**Explicitly open, and this ticket's first shaping question:** whether "the partner never captures" is one model or several (agency vs. net-rate vs. consignment). Those settle differently and the choice is the owner's, not a planner's.

**Non-goals:** the credential model itself (ADR-056, shipped), availability reads (shipped), invoicing/B2B terms (TKT-34).

Quality gates: `make check`; money paths integer minor units.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by the 2026-08-25 backlog review. TKT-240's closeout named this the largest remaining piece — *"a larger piece of work than everything else in this ticket"* — and handed it to **TKT-23**, an epic that is not decomposed. That is a real gap in the board rather than in the code: the reseller API reads as delivered while its selling half is absent.

**Not ready, and should not be forced.** The settlement model is a product decision that changes ADR-048, and shaping should expect at least one `owner: human` item (which reseller commercial model) plus probably a spike on the ledger shape. Recommend it be shaped as a child of TKT-23 if the owner decomposes that epic, rather than run standalone.

**Needs shaping before Gate 1.**
